correctness.rationale: The orbit count follows from the rank-one factorization and free scalar action. Fixing a standard nilpotent, a=s_2 and b=t_1 give the exact commutator, rank conditions and diagonalizability, including characteristic two. Two independent linear constraints yield \(q^{2n-3}\) partners for each nonzero trace and \(q^{n-1}(q^{n-2}-1)\) for each one-sided rank-one case. Lie brackets [C,X]=2λX and [C,Y]=-2λY prove the generation classification, with a separate linear-independence check. The standalone finite-field program confirms nine configurations; these experiments corroborate rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The minimal nilpotent conjugacy orbit is a canonical, naturally defined family, not an arbitrary slice. The finding gives its full commutator rank distribution, each nonzero trace stratum, ordered-pair frequencies and Lie-generation types for every matrix dimension and finite field, exhibits the sharp \(n=2\) rank-one-stratum threshold, and isolates the characteristic-two collapse of \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) to a Heisenberg Lie algebra. The invariants address the interplay of Lie generation and finite-field incidence across a parameterized family.
